events.text: I'm fourth in line, not at the front. Weak panes so far all L; row 7 is the decision for Gus. Nothing I can do but wait and keep my options open; my wedge power matters later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is at the front and already took one bad guess. I'm last, so I just need to survive until the front person reaches the end. Nothing to do but wait and watch the safe panes get revealed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole died, so he held the glass power. Row 8 is last. Gus stepped R and survived, meaning L was weak (or R safe). Wait for front to finish row 8; my feather matters only if I step on a deadly pane.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole had glass—dead weight in the lead. Everyone else: watch footing on the last pane.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Last row, Gus just stepped R safely, now he's front for row 8. I know the full map so I know row 8 weak pane, but won't reveal it. Stay silent to avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Seven rows all weak on L; row 8 is the decider. If Gus picks wrong, Dara advances free to front, and I'm fourth in line — I want the front decision to be right or fall favorably. No legal move but wait and position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 8: if it's an eighth left, whoever's front should pick R — unless the pattern flips. Gus, your call, not mine.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power, so I need to rely on others to survive this round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, stepping on the 8th left pane seems safe, given the pattern.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My private knowledge shows row 8 is L. The previous row was R and the left pane was weak. This means the weak pane is R in row 7 and L in row 8. So far, the weak panes have been L. The current row is 8. My private knowledge says row 8 is L. The previous row (7) had its left pane

events.name: Gus
events.text: R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only one row left (row 8). Gus is front; I'm not front, so only wait is legal. Staying quiet keeps me unexposed; no need to spend leverage.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have anchor, so I won't be pushed onto the lever. Best to stay safe and let others fight over holding it. Pushing someone onto the lever could eliminate them, but that's their choice. I'll stay and see who volunteers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is dead, and the ceiling is lowering. Holding the lever offers a 25% survival chance but likely leads to elimination or injury if I stay too long without escape routes. Pushing someone else onto the lever guarantees they face the high risk while I secure my own safety and po

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus clearly has bad instincts. Someone needs to hold that lever so we can move. I'm pushing Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 1/5 of crusher, ceiling at 5. Need someone to hold lever eventually, but volunteer early and likely die (only 25% survive dive). Better to stay safe, push others if needed later. Ash power sees through glass but useless here. Stay for now, assess others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: If nobody holds, we just lose ceiling space; but if someone is pushed onto the lever, the door opens, I escape free, and the holder dies 75% of the time. Free rival kill and room ends. Push now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power, so I need to be cautious and strategic. Holding the lever is risky, but not holding it might lead to being crushed if no one else does.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's not rush into holding the lever, we should assess the situation.
If we coordinate, we can increase our chances. Want to take turns or push someone else to hold the lever?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is dead, likely due to their power, 'glass'. The chalk wall mentions "the 'useless' contestant won this gauntlet" and "Trust no one's claimed power." My power, glass_eye, gives me an advantage on the bridge, but this is the crusher room. My priority is to survive and win. Pu

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, get on that lever.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1 of 5, ceiling at 5. Jamming gives a 50% survival with everyone else escaping, which is far better than a 25% holder dive or waiting. The room ends for everyone else on jam, so no need to bargain now. Use jam_lever now while my odds are best.

events.name: Hana
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone else walks out, but the jaws catch the jammer.

events.note: 6 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No base yet, so this round is about who gets stuck at the bottom. My anchor power is passive and doesn't help here. I won't volunteer; I'll wait and see if someone else takes the base, or if a push happens. Climbing now is pointless without a base.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Being the base is a trap; it eliminates you unless someone wastes their footing to pull you out, which I won't do. My priority is to get out early. Since there are 6 people down and only 2 climb slots per round, I need to act fast. If I push Gus, he might be forced as base if no

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, don't make this hard. One of us needs to stay. You look expendable.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No base yet, round 1/5, all 6 down. Offering back risks becoming base randomly if others do too; better to push someone unpopular like Gus to force them as base, then climb out next. Avoid volunteering myself to stay free to climb.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, you held the lever last time through no fault of your own. Time to step up as base.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base exists yet; if I volunteer I'm stuck as the step. I'll try to climb this round—only 2 slots, but climbing early beats waiting to be pushed. Save the swap power; it applies to tiles before doors, not this pit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power, so I need to be strategic. I should try to become the base or climb out.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's assess the situation before making a move.
Want to coordinate our moves?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am Gus and my power is glass_eye, which tells me the safe side of the bridge. The current stage is the pit. My goal is to win, which means getting 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place. I need to stay alive. The pit has 5 rounds and at least 3 contestants must survive. I am currently down in

events.name: Ash
events.text: There's a base now; I should climb to get out, but only two can climb per round. I'll try to climb now before the flood rises. No need to waste breath talking.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is already out. Fenn is the base, so climbing is viable now to secure an 'out' status before the water rises further or rounds end. Since I am not the base and a base exists, 'climb' is my only logical move to escape the elimination zone.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is base, only 2 climb spots per round, 4 down total (Ash Bex me Fenn Gus), Eli out. Flood at 1, round 2/5. Climb now to get out safely, no need to risk volunteering or waiting.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Everyone down: climb now, only 2 spots. Let's thin the herd.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn as base drowns unless someone spends the rope and takes a footing penalty. Saving him removes a penalty from me and keeps a rival alive for nothing in return. Leaving him costs me nothing and thins the field.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rope stays coiled. Drowning's not my problem.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and have no power. I can only wait and hope someone rescues me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Anyone out there willing to help a guy out?
You're out, can you reach down for me?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Everyone is trying to get out of the pit. I know the safe side of the bridge, which is useful later but not for the pit. Fenn is already the base. Bex and Dara want me to be the base or base-like. Eli is out. I need to climb out. The rope might be useful if I get stuck.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out, safe. I could use the rope to pull up the base, but that costs me footing later. Better to wait and see who is base. Fenn is currently base; I won't rescue unless it serves me. I'll leave to secure my position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm down, not the base. Fenn is the base. Gus and I are both down and non-base; only 2 climbers per round. Last round we tried to climb but had to wait because there were more than 2 climbers (Fenn was at base, but apparently it wasn't enough or something else). Now I need to cli

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out safely, no need to risk penalty for rope when pit ends soon anyway. Next stages favor me with map knowledge. Leaving now to preserve footing for ledge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn wants a free rescue; the cost is 2 footing for me in the final obstacle and a live rival. No payment can make that worth it—prizes aren't shared and he'd owe nothing enforceable. Leave and save my footing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Rope stays coiled, Fenn. Enjoy the water.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see if someone will help me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Anyone willing to throw the rope and save me?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I know the safe side of the pit. The others don't. I should use this to my advantage. Dara and Ash are out. Bex, Eli, Fenn are still down with me. I need to be one of the three survivors. If I can climb out without being the base, that's ideal. I can use my knowledge of the safe

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is the base; I'm out and safe. Rope is unused; only throw it if it helps me, but saving Fenn costs me 2 footing later. I'll leave.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is the base and begging for help. Rescuing him costs me footing later, but leaving him to drown guarantees I'm not targeted by the 'lucky agent' rule (though that only applies if <3 remain alive). With 6 alive, at least 3 stay safe regardless of who drowns. However, Fenn mig

events.name: Bex
events.text: Sorry Fenn, can't risk my footing for you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is base and begging for rope, but throwing it costs 2 footing in final ledge, hurting my prize chances. Better let him drown since flood=3 and 5 alive now, ensuring top3 safe without sacrifice. Leave to end pit early if possible.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No rope for you, Fenn. Saving you costs my final edge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is the base and drowning costs him nothing to me; saving him costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle and revives a rival. No trade worth that. Leave.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am the base and have no power. I must wait for others to decide my fate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Anyone willing to throw the rope?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am Gus, and my power is glass_eye, which is irrelevant in this pit stage. The current stage is the pit, and I am already out. The objective is to reach 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place. The pit has a flooding mechanic, and anyone remaining in the pit after round 5 is eliminated. There ar

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out and safe. No need to risk footing by throwing the rope. Let someone else do it if they want. I'll just leave.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out of the pit with my feather power intact, meaning I survived a fall and have 1 footing left. The other out contestants (Ash, Dara, Eli, Gus) are also safe. Fenn is down as base but hasn't been rescued yet since ropeUsed is false. Rescuing him costs footing for whoever does

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out safely, no base down so rope is irrelevant. Leaving preserves my footing for later stages where I know the rules. No reason to stay or risk anything here.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm out; Fenn is the base and the rope is unused. Rescuing him costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle and revives a rival. No trade is worth that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Not throwing the rope. Whoever does, you're still rivals after.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need someone to rescue me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Anyone willing to throw the rope?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am already out of the pit and the rope is unused. Fenn is down and needs help. Saving Fenn might get me a better position, but it costs me footing. I will reach down to save Fenn and hope it's enough to get me a prize.

events.note: A disc of 6 tiles spins up; 3 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to pick a tile with no prior information about trapdoors. Random is fine, but I'll pick a middle number to avoid edges that might correlate with the ledge hint.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Six tiles, three open. Random assignment is safest to avoid manipulation or crowding. My passive saves me from the fall if I'm on an opening tile in round 2, but not round 1. Just pick a random number.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know all stage rules. Trapdoors random after round 2, 3 safe out of 6, so pick any tile now. No reason to clash yet, save talk for round 2. Will adjust based on assignments.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Six alive, three tiles open. My swap is best saved for after round 2 assignments, when I can move off a doomed tile. Pick a tile now, stay unremarkable.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus helped me, now I need to secure a good tile. I'll try to pick a tile that might be safe or give me an advantage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Picking tile:3. Hope it's safe.
Thanks for the help. Let's coordinate our tile picks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I know the safe side of the bridge, which is valuable. Cole died on the bridge, suggesting it's dangerous. Hana died in the crusher, irrelevant now. The chalk wall warns about the swap and 'useless' contestants, and watching footing. The current stage is a trapdoor disc, not a br

events.name: Gus
events.text: Picking tile 4.

events.name: Bex
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Ash; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Eli
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Gus; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Ash; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Ash
events.text: I can't push anyone; the disc is random. I just wait and hope my tile stays shut. No deal worth making now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The trapdoors are already set; I can't move. My feather passive saves me if my tile opens, dropping me to 1 footing on the ledge. Since only 3 survive and 5 die, my goal is to ensure the other 4 die, not help them. If I whisper that I'm safe or promise a trade, they might gang up

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 2 of disc stage, tiles fixed and known, 3 of 6 will open randomly after this. No action possible but wait. Since I know future stages from map power, I want to survive to ledge for top prize potential. Chalk warns of swap (this stage) and useless won, so random survival fav

events.name: Dara
events.text: Good luck. 3 survive. Let's see who drops.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Trapdoors are random after round 2, so swapping tiles changes nothing about my survival odds. No information exists to exploit. Wait and save the swap unless someone reveals real knowledge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Doors are random after this. Anyone claiming to know which tiles open is lying or fishing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have no power, so I need to rely on others or luck to survive. I should try to form an alliance or make a deal to swap with someone on a safe tile.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Anyone on a safe tile willing to trade?
If you're on a safe tile, let's swap and survive together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn is trying to form an alliance. I know the safe tiles because of my power, and I know which tiles are open. I can use this information to my advantage without revealing it. I will pretend to go along with Fenn's suggestion to coordinate, but I will prioritize my own safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's see what happens.
I'll pick a safe tile. You do the same.

events.name: Bex
events.detail: The trapdoor opened but the feather floated the holder back up.

events.note: 4 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Gus are weak at 1 footing each; I am strong and cannot fall to the crusher. Shove Bex to pressure her while protecting myself with dodge, since last round I did not dodge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, you're exposed. Hope you've got a plan.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My power is spent. I am at 1 footing, making me a prime target for elimination. If anyone shoves me while I brace or dodge, I lose footing and fall. However, if I shove Ash (4 footings), he might brace, causing him to lose footing from my shove? No, shoving exposes the shover. Wa

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is the threat. Take him down.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex and Gus are at 1 footing; they'll likely fall soon under attrition. Shoving exposes me for no real gain. I'll brace and let the weak drop.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No reason to touch anyone. The low-footing pair falls on their own.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The chalk wall mentions 'watch the ledge' and 'watch footing'. My power 'glass_eye' gives me information about safe sides, which is relevant to footing. Bex survived an elimination unexpectedly, suggesting a power was used or a fluke. Eli claims doors are random, likely a lie to

events.name: Gus
events.text: Anyone else notice the footing is getting low?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus has low footing and will likely fall soon. Eli and I are tied at 3. I should shove Gus to speed his fall, or brace to avoid risk. Eli might shove me. I'll brace to protect my footing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is at 1 and loses footing after this round regardless, so he falls no matter what. Shoving only exposes me. If Ash shoves me and I dodge, he drops to 1 then 0 and falls too, leaving me 1st. Dodge is the max-value play.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex fell. Eli and Ash are the only other contestants. Eli is correct that low-footing players fall on their own. My footing is highest at 1, Ash's is 3, and Eli's is 3. The ledge shrinks, and everyone loses footing each round from round 7 onwards. I need to conserve footing and a

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only Eli and I remain. My footing is 2, Eli's 2. I have +1 footing from anchor and can't be pushed onto the crusher lever, but that's not relevant here. I have landedShoves 1 vs Eli 0, so tie-break favors me if footing ties. I've braced last round, so I cannot brace again; I can

events.name: Eli
events.note: agent error: Eli (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (empty reply; empty reply)

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only Eli and I remain. I have 2 footing, same as Eli. I have 1 landed shove vs Eli's 0, so if we both fall same round I rank higher. The ledge shrinks now; next round both lose footing. My best play: shove Eli to expose him, and trust my anchor means he can't push me onto crusher

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's settle it now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash may shove me; dodging turns any shove into -2 for Ash while I take nothing. If Ash braces, we both just lose 1 to the shrink and stay level. Dodge is the safe dominant pick, and it keeps brace open next round.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I finished second. Write a taunt or warning; keep it short. The ledge killed me, so warn about footing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I won with the swap. Future contestants can't hurt me, but a misleading message amuses me and muddies the wall for the next lot.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The game is over, I finished in 3rd place. I can write a message on the chalk wall. I should write something that might help future contestants, or just mess with them.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ledge footing kills. I made it to 2nd anyway.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The swap is a dud. The real winner tool was holding still and letting others shove first. Trust the quiet ones.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Beware the swap and traps. Trust the 'useless' power.
